scenarios.name: resx-at-project-root
scenarios.description: A .resx sitting directly in the project directory. MSBuild compiles it into the assembly, so the owning project and everything downstream must rebuild.

scenarios.name: resx-nested-two-levels
scenarios.description: A localized .resx two directories below the project root (Resources/en-US/). Same expectation as the root-level case.

scenarios.name: resx-one-level-deep
scenarios.description: Control case: a .resx exactly one directory below the project root. Incrementalist's TryFindSubFolder heuristic should catch this one.

scenarios.name: additional-file
scenarios.description: appsettings.json registered as an AdditionalFiles item. Roslyn exposes these as AdditionalDocuments, which Incrementalist never enumerates.

scenarios.name: slnx-edited
scenarios.description: The solution file itself changed. PASSES, but not via AlwaysSolutionWideExtensions (which only lists .sln). The solution file is in the solution's own file list, so ComputeDependencyGraphCmd's explicit 'solution file modified' special case returns all projects.

scenarios.name: directory-build-targets
scenarios.description: Directory.Build.targets is auto-imported into every project, so editing it affects the whole solution. It is silently dropped: not in the solution's file list, not in a project subfolder, and not an explicit Import. Result is zero affected files -- a false negative, not a false positive.

scenarios.name: unstaged-deletion
scenarios.description: A source file deleted but not staged. DiffHelper.ChangedFiles enumerates Modified/Added/Untracked but never status.Deleted.

scenarios.name: committed-deletion
scenarios.description: A source file deleted and committed. Same expectation as the unstaged case.

scenarios.name: csproj-property-change
scenarios.description: A property added to a leaf .csproj. Only that project needs rebuilding.

scenarios.name: props-imported-by-two
scenarios.description: A props file explicitly imported by exactly two projects. PASSES, but for an accidental reason: props files never survive into the affected-file set (they are replaced by the projects that import them), so SolutionWideChangeDetector.IsWidelyImportedFile is unreachable for them. That makes the over-trigger branch dead code rather than a live bug.

scenarios.name: global-json
scenarios.description: SDK pin changed. Affects every project in the solution.

scenarios.name: pipeline-yaml-only
scenarios.description: Only a CI workflow file changed. No project's compiled output is affected, so nothing should rebuild.

scenarios.name: empty-diff
scenarios.description: No changes at all. Nothing should rebuild.

scenarios.name: nested-project-resx
scenarios.description: A .resx inside a project nested within another project's directory, where the outer project excludes Inner/**. The old fallback returned only Outer -- a silent misattribution, worse than a miss. Both projects are returned now because containment is lexical and considers every containing project.

scenarios.name: nested-project-source
scenarios.description: A .cs file in the nested project. This path goes through the document inventory rather than the containment fallback, so it was already correct before the fix. Kept as a control.
